newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries rise in London, FOMC talk dominates.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries rise in London, FOMC talk dominates.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London were higher on Wednesday after weakening overnight and in early trade on talk of an interest rate rise at next week's FOMC meeting, traders and analysts said.

Market sentiment was nervous after a Fed source told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that eight of the 12 Fed banks had requested an increase in interest rates at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on September 24.
"Yesterday's story shifts the balance back towards a Fed tightening on the 24th," said Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International in London.

"It caused yields to rise across the curve particularly at the short end," said Chester. "There's been further weakness overnight and in London and the long-bond is trading back above seven percent, with the two-year above 6.20."
The 30-year benchmark bond was trading at 96-23 by 1014 GMT, to yield 7.013 percent, compared with 96.21 in Tokyo and 96.18 in New York.
Two-year T-notes were at 99-26, versus 99-25 in Tokyo and 99-24 in New York.
Five-year T-notes were at 99-19, unchanged from Tokyo and up 3/32 from New York, while 10-year T-bonds were at 101-10, compared with 101-09 in Tokyo and 101-06 in New York.

A trader at a U.S. bank in London said the market had been better bid at the lower levels to which the market fell in early London trade, with buying for Far East and British accounts primarily at the two-, five- and 10-year maturities.
Following the story on Tuesday, there had been a correction in the market with the two-year sector coming off 10 to 15 basis points, he said.
"The curve flattened and that was the right trade. It could flatten a few more basis points," he said.
He said there were some swap deals due to take place later in the session which might give the market a slightly better bid.
Chester said the market had been whipsawed since last Friday when the weak consumer price and retail sales data was released.

"People read into that that the Fed would probably stay on hold, but judging by yesterday's story the Fed are looking beyond just the coincidental inflation data and are seeking to re-establish their pre-emptive credentials," Chester said.
The U.S bank trader said following the story, there had been a correction in the market with the two-year sector coming off 10 to 15 basis points.
Analysts said the U.S. July trade balance to be released at 1230 GMT, would not have a major impact on the market.
The forecast is for a fall of 8.8 billion, compared with a previous fall of 8.1 billion.
At 1014 GMT, December T-bond futures were at 108-02 in automated trade, down 2/32 from Tuesday's Chicago settlement.
